7J52mDjZzto.summary: Technology Connections explains how heat pumps work as reversed air conditioners and why they can deliver several times the heat of resistive heating per unit of energy. It also tackles common myths such as poor cold-weather performance.
7J52mDjZzto.why: HN's default recommendation for a friendly, thorough introduction to heat pumps and why they are so efficient.

7Pq-S557XQU.summary: CGP Grey's video "Humans Need Not Apply" argues that automation will make a large part of the workforce economically obsolete, much as engines did for horses. It surveys robots and software replacing both physical and mental labor.
7Pq-S557XQU.why: HN has recommended it for a decade as the standard explainer on automation and unemployment, though skeptics later cite it as an example of overconfident predictions.

7IsMeKl-Sv0.summary: Not Just Bikes explains the Strong Towns argument that car-dependent American suburbs cost more to maintain than they generate in taxes. It describes the growth Ponzi scheme that props up municipal finances.
7IsMeKl-Sv0.why: HN keeps pointing to it as the clearest explanation of how low-density infrastructure is financed and why it is unsustainable.

7xTGNNLPyMI.summary: Andrej Karpathy's three-hour-plus general-audience deep dive into how ChatGPT-style LLMs are built, covering the full training stack from pretraining to post-training. It also gives mental models for their quirks, like hallucination, and how to use them well.
7xTGNNLPyMI.why: HN's most frequent recommendation for a clear, approachable foundation in how LLMs work without heavy math.

7rNY7xKyGCQ.summary: Dr. Michael Greger presents his book How Not to Die at Google NYC, arguing that diet and lifestyle changes can prevent or reverse many of the top causes of death. He walks through evidence on whole-food plant-based eating.
7rNY7xKyGCQ.why: Frequently recommended in threads on nutrition, cancer and veganism as a science-focused case for plant-based diets, with at least one commenter saying it made them go vegan.

7Hk9jct2ozY.summary: A compilation of molecular animations of DNA replication and gene transcription by Drew Berry and Etsuko Uno at WEHI, made with no narration. It shows molecular machinery at work inside cells.
7Hk9jct2ozY.why: Recommended whenever people want to see the mechanical, jostling reality of molecular biology, which many find awe-inspiring.

7EmboKQH8lM.summary: The first lesson of Uncle Bob (Robert C. Martin)'s "Coding Better World Together" series. It makes the case for clean code and for treating software craftsmanship as an ethical and professional responsibility. It runs about 109 minutes.
7EmboKQH8lM.why: HN commenters call it better than the Clean Code book, a must-watch for engineers that changes how they read and write code.

7ImvlS8PLIo.summary: Lawrence Krauss's 2009 talk on the current picture of the universe, how it will end and how it could have come from nothing. It covers the expanding universe, cosmic background radiation and the cosmological constant.
7ImvlS8PLIo.why: HN regards it as a famous, mesmerizing talk, especially for the point that distant galaxies will become unobservable.

7ttG90raCNo.summary: VFX supervisor Jonas Ussing examines what studios mean by "no CGI", showing how much invisible CGI hides behind practical-effects marketing. It is the first part of a multi-part series that includes analysis of doctored behind-the-scenes footage.
7ttG90raCNo.why: Strongly recommended whenever HN discusses CGI, practical effects, or trusting behind-the-scenes footage.

7jiPeIFXb6U.summary: Joel Grus's JupyterCon talk explaining why he dislikes Jupyter notebooks. He covers hidden state, trouble with reproducibility and testing, and how notebooks frustrate teaching. He shows his preferred workflow and what Jupyter could change.
7jiPeIFXb6U.why: It is the go-to funny, irreverent critique of notebooks, linked whenever HN debates notebooks versus testable code.

7vfqkvwW2fs.summary: An Every Frame a Painting video essay asking why Marvel films lack memorable musical themes. It blames temp tracks and directors scoring to filler music.
7vfqkvwW2fs.why: HN recommends it as an insightful explanation of why modern film scores sound alike, with lessons beyond Marvel.

7zrx-b2sLUs.summary: A Technology Connections video on how ground-source (geothermal) heat pumps work and why they hold efficiency in winter. It also covers related heat pump information, and the description notes air-source heat pumps have since improved.
7zrx-b2sLUs.why: Recommended as part of an excellent, approachable series explaining residential heat pumps.

7FeqF1-Z1g0.summary: David Kriesel's 31C3 talk, in German, on the discovery that Xerox scanner-copiers silently replace digits and letters in scanned documents. He explains how the bug stayed unnoticed in the wild for years.
7FeqF1-Z1g0.why: Called a classic CCC talk, and the Xerox bug is cited as a cautionary tale about trusting scans and digitized archives.

7erJ1DV_Tlo.summary: A standing whiteboard conversation at Lang.NEXT 2012 among Carl Hewitt, Erik Meijer and Clemens Szyperski about the actor model. Hewitt, who originated the model, explains its foundations.
7erJ1DV_Tlo.why: HN recommends it as the best video introduction to the actor model, straight from its inventor, and revisited it after Hewitt's death.

79fvDDPaIoY.summary: Bryan Cantrill of Joyent presents Manta, an internet-facing object store that lets you run compute directly on the data. The talk is peppered with ZFS history and Cantrill's trademark commentary on the industry.
79fvDDPaIoY.why: HN recommends Cantrill talks generally for their mix of industry history, technical depth and entertaining delivery, and this one is a favorite for storage and data integrity threads.

72y2EC5fkcE.summary: Allan Blomquist demonstrates the internal programming and debugging tools Tomorrow Corporation uses to make games, including live modification of a running game and time-travel debugging.
72y2EC5fkcE.why: Held up in debugger and tooling threads as an amazing ideal of a tight feedback loop and what debugging could be.

7G4ipM2qjfw.summary: Practical Engineering explains why connecting solar and other inverter-based generation to the grid is hard. It covers grid stability, load balancing and the behind-the-scenes engineering challenges of renewables.
7G4ipM2qjfw.why: HN people link it as the go-to explainer for grid and inverter stability, especially in threads about blackouts and distributed solar.

7J7X7aZvMXQ.summary: A 36-minute animated deep dive from Branch Education into how DRAM works. It shows how memory connects to the CPU and how billions of bits are stored in nanoscale capacitor cells. It also covers why DRAM sits between SSDs and the processor.
7J7X7aZvMXQ.why: Commenters recommend it as a clear, well-animated explanation of memory, especially for visual learners.

7NfX0vlCa4k.summary: Technology Connections gives first impressions of using an Onyx Boox Max2 e-ink tablet for productivity, including using it as an external display. He shows what the device can and cannot do.
7NfX0vlCa4k.why: HN recommends it, with its companion video, as an honest hands-on account of e-ink devices as monitors, including their slow software and limits.

7Nw6qyyrTeI.summary: Not Just Bikes explains, using Urban3's property-tax analysis, why car-dependent suburbs generate less tax revenue than they cost to maintain, so dense urban cores effectively subsidize them. It is part of a Strong Towns series.
7Nw6qyyrTeI.why: The go-to link in urban planning threads for the claim that suburban infrastructure costs more per resident than it pays back.

7jb0FOcImdg.summary: A 2018 GDC talk by NetherRealm's Michael Stallone on the engine changes, optimizations and tooling needed to roll back and re-simulate up to 8 frames in 16 ms in Mortal Kombat and Injustice 2. It is a deep dive into deterministic rollback netcode.
7jb0FOcImdg.why: HN treats it as the definitive practical talk on rollback networking in a shipped AAA fighting game.

7y1xJAVZxXg.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on televangelists and the 'seed faith' prosperity gospel. It looks at how US tax law lets preachers extract money from poor viewers, and how easy it is to start a church.
7y1xJAVZxXg.why: HN cites it in threads on churches, tax exemption and religious fundraising, as the go-to explainer on seed faith televangelism.

7QmCUDHpNzE.summary: The original five-minute Dropbox demo video, which presented the product's features before a finished product existed. It was aimed at technical early adopters and became famous as a launch strategy.
7QmCUDHpNzE.why: HN cites it as the classic example of validating a product idea with a demo video, and many recall how compelling it was.

7g1Acy5eGbE.summary: Emery Berger argues that performance is hard to measure and deliver on modern systems, showing how code layout and link order can swamp optimization effects. He presents tools that evaluate performance more reliably.
7g1Acy5eGbE.why: HN points to it whenever benchmarking pitfalls and layout effects come up, as an eye-opening talk on how unreliable naive measurements are.

7CgXvIuZR40.summary: A recording of the TASBot block at Awesome Games Done Quick 2017, where a robot plays games via tool-assisted speedruns, including Super Mario 64 and Portal on an SNES via arbitrary code execution, and ending with a Twitch Plays segment. It showcases console exploits and creative hardware hacking.
7CgXvIuZR40.why: HN commenters rate it a great GDQ watch and point to its feats, such as streaming video and Skype through controller ports, as inspiring hacks.

7HKbjYqqPPQ.summary: Guy Steele's PPoPP 2017 keynote surveying the history of computer science metanotation, including BNF, inference rules, and overline notation. He argues the field's notations are inconsistent and fragmented.
7HKbjYqqPPQ.why: HN recommends it as an excellent talk on notation problems, useful when reading papers or designing a new metalanguage.

7OpM_zKGE4o.summary: Real Engineering looks at why Africa's abundant solar potential is hard to turn into usable power, especially for Europe. It covers the transmission, infrastructure and economic obstacles, and the pivot from concentrated solar to photovoltaics.
7OpM_zKGE4o.why: Linked whenever commenters ask whether Sahara solar could power Europe, as a clear explanation of why it is impractical.

72cM_E6bsOs.summary: PBS Space Time explains the Hubble constant tension, in which two precise, independent methods of measuring the universe's expansion rate disagree. It covers why this calls some standard cosmology into question.
72cM_E6bsOs.why: Recommended as a clear, layman-friendly explanation of the Hubble tension from a channel regarded well by physicists.

74zOY-vgkyw.summary: The first stream in the Emacs From Scratch series, building a custom Emacs configuration from zero while teaching basics. It covers a usable baseline setup and the packages for completion, themes and productivity.
74zOY-vgkyw.why: Recommended as a thoughtful, step-by-step way to build your own Emacs config rather than starting from Doom or Spacemacs.

7JUs4c99-mo.summary: A talk by Yuri Iozzelli at a WebAssembly meetup on CheerpX, an x86 virtual machine running in the browser. It uses a JIT compiler that emits WebAssembly at runtime to run real native applications. It covers the architecture and demos such as porting a multiplayer C++ game.
7JUs4c99-mo.why: HN points to it as an impressive look at how far WebAssembly can go, and as the explanation of the architecture behind CheerpX and its Flash support.

7gDKbT_l2us.summary: A roughly 90-minute video essay by ContraPoints on J.K. Rowling and the controversy around her views on gender. It examines why many LGBTQ people and allies soured on her.
7gDKbT_l2us.why: HN recommends it as a thorough, nuanced perspective on the Rowling controversy and on cancel culture from a trans creator.

7hwO8Q_TyCA.summary: Dave Ackley gives a high-level introduction to robust-first computing, which prioritizes robustness over efficiency in computer architecture. A sorting demo illustrates the idea.
7hwO8Q_TyCA.why: HN recommends it as a short, clear explanation of robust-first computing by its originator, and as a philosophy relevant to building with unreliable components like LLMs.

7kGnfXXIKZM.summary: Ophthalmologist Chris Knobbe argues that excess omega-6 seed oils are a unifying cause of chronic diseases of civilization such as diabetes and macular degeneration. He presents the case at Low Carb Denver 2020.
7kGnfXXIKZM.why: HN commenters point to it in nutrition threads as the strongest case against seed oils, though it is a contested claim.

7Q25-S7jzgs.summary: Larry Lessig's TED talk argues that copyright law chokes creativity, drawing on John Philip Sousa, celestial copyrights and the ASCAP cartel to make the case for reviving remix culture.
7Q25-S7jzgs.why: Recommended in copyright, patent and SOPA threads as a clear case for copyright reform.

7R4xhwy-1oI.summary: Susan Crawford talks at Harvard's Berkman Klein Center about her book Captive Audience. She argues that deregulation and consolidation left a few telecom companies in control of American internet access, so people pay too much for slow service.
7R4xhwy-1oI.why: Recommended in broadband and net neutrality threads as an overview of the US telecom monopoly problem.

7ZGCPap7GkY.summary: A Google Tech Talk by Sebastian Deterding on gamification. It looks at what points and badges get wrong and what lessons game design offers for non-game applications.
7ZGCPap7GkY.why: HN commenters recommend it as a thoughtful take on doing gamification and game design well.

7ZVWIELHQQY.summary: A clip of Craig Ferguson's late-night monologue in which he talks about his past as an alcoholic. He explains why he will not mock Britney Spears over her breakdown.
7ZVWIELHQQY.why: HN users share it in threads on drinking and addiction as an honest account of alcoholism and sobriety.

7kVeCqQCxlk.summary: Morten Rand-Hendriksen's WordCamp Europe 2017 talk presents CSS Grid Layout as a native two-dimensional layout system that changes how web pages are structured, including responsive layouts independent of source order. It was given as browsers began shipping support.
7kVeCqQCxlk.why: HN commenters recommend it as an inspiring demonstration of how powerful CSS Grid is and how it repairs the relationship between HTML and CSS.

7nJgHBbEgsE.summary: Dr. Jason Fung's talk at the 2018 CrossFit Health Conference on therapeutic fasting for weight loss. He explains why long-term weight loss is hard and tackles common myths.
7nJgHBbEgsE.why: HN people point to Fung as the best resource for understanding fasting and weight loss.

7pSqk-XV2QM.summary: Veritasium tells how Kodak film was fogged by radioactive fallout from the first atomic tests, letting the company detect nuclear testing before anyone announced it. The video also covers the deal to keep it quiet and how fallout contaminated packaging.
7pSqk-XV2QM.why: HN commenters bring it up as a good related watch in any thread about fallout, nuclear tests or detecting hidden events through indirect evidence.

7tsXtk7psUc.summary: Serpentza, a Westerner living in China, describes Chinese influence efforts abroad and the cultural conflict between Shen Yun and Confucius Institutes. It is a commentary from his personal perspective.
7tsXtk7psUc.why: HN commenters recommend it as an interesting on-the-ground perspective on Confucius Institutes and Chinese influence operations.

7vsCAM17O-M.summary: CGP Grey argues that a classroom works well only for the one student pitched at the average level, and sketches a future of personalized instruction. It introduces the idea of a Digital Aristotle, a tutor for every learner.
7vsCAM17O-M.why: Brought up in nearly every discussion of AI tutors and the future of schooling as the original Digital Aristotle idea.

7wC42HgLA4k.summary: A short CGP Grey animation showing how the US electoral college lets a candidate win the presidency with as little as about 22 percent of the popular vote. It lays out the arithmetic of winning states by narrow margins.
7wC42HgLA4k.why: Linked in electoral-system discussions as a quick, clear argument against the electoral college.

77IdKFqXbUY.summary: A short video of Robert F. Kennedy's 1968 speech criticizing Gross Domestic Product as a measure of progress, saying it counts everything except what makes life worthwhile.
77IdKFqXbUY.why: Quoted in economics threads about growth, work and basic income as a classic critique of GDP.

7Hlb8YX2-W8.summary: A long livestream of George Hotz live-coding a toy SLAM implementation, twitchslam, over two days in May 2018. It is an unedited session of Python programming with computer vision and visualization.
7Hlb8YX2-W8.why: Recommended as informal, long-form live coding to watch, though some commenters criticize his style.

7LqaotiGWjQ.summary: Daniel Schmachtenberger discusses why the information ecology is damaged and what healthy public sensemaking would take. The conversation ties this to the meaning crisis and to improving discourse.
7LqaotiGWjQ.why: Recommended to people interested in propaganda, misinformation and how to improve public discourse.

7S-DGTBZU14.summary: A Jimquisition episode examining the human cost of predatory videogame monetization, focusing on loot boxes and microtransactions. It features testimonials from people harmed by gambling-style game mechanics.
7S-DGTBZU14.why: Pointed to in threads on loot boxes, gacha games and exploitative monetization as a damning overview.

7VG_s2PCH_c.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on vaccines, arguing that the benefits far outweigh the minuscule risks and discussing why some parents still doubt their safety.
7VG_s2PCH_c.why: HN recommends it as an accessible, funny explanation of why vaccines matter.

7Vc8sxhy2I4.summary: Mikey Dickerson's keynote at Velocity NY 2014, one year after the healthcare.gov launch failure. He recounts how a small team rescued the site and what the episode showed about government IT contracting.
7Vc8sxhy2I4.why: HN cites it as a firsthand account of how dysfunctional large IT projects can be, with about 50 contractors and no one in charge.

7gtog_gOaGQ.summary: Professor Ruzic explains modular micro-reactors: self-contained nuclear units with passive safety whose fuel lasts about 20 years. He covers their use for process and district heat and where they can compete with diesel generation.
7gtog_gOaGQ.why: Recommended as a clear technical explanation of micro-reactor fuel, safety and economics, from a channel HN trusts on nuclear topics.

7ne0GArfeMs.summary: Terence Tao's AMS Einstein Public Lecture at UCLA on the cosmic distance ladder, the chain of methods astronomers use to measure distances from the Earth to distant galaxies. It is aimed at a general audience.
7ne0GArfeMs.why: HN recommends it as an accessible and elegant tour of how indirect reasoning builds up cosmic measurements, with one commenter calling it their favorite Tao work.

7oWip00iXbo.summary: Physicist Jacob Barandes discusses his view that quantum mechanics can be formulated without wave functions, using a stochastic, probabilistic approach. The long interview covers measurement, the foundations of quantum theory and the history of the field.
7oWip00iXbo.why: HN commenters point to it as a credible, clearly explained alternative take on quantum foundations from a Harvard physicist.

7xQQkzWhMOc.summary: An episode of Patriot Act with Hasan Minhaj exposing how tax-prep companies like TurboTax make filing confusing and costly even though many Americans can file for free. It combines comedy with reporting on lobbying and dark patterns.
7xQQkzWhMOc.why: HN recommends it as an accessible explanation of how Intuit's lobbying and deceptive design undermine free tax filing.

783ccP__No8.summary: A documentary on how GraphQL came to be at Facebook, featuring its co-creators Lee Byron, Dan Schafer and Nick Schrock. It covers the problems it solved and its adoption at companies like Twitter, Airbnb and GitHub.
783ccP__No8.why: HN recommends it for understanding the original motivation behind GraphQL before judging whether it fits your problem.

7N41TEcjcvM.summary: A two-minute demonstration of LucasArts' iMUSE adaptive music system in Monkey Island 2. It shows music layers and transitions changing seamlessly as the player moves.
7N41TEcjcvM.why: HN points to it as the clearest short demo of iMUSE, considered a high point in video game music.

7PKx3kS7f4A.summary: Rob Miles explains for Computerphile why simple rule sets like Asimov's Three Laws cannot make robots and AI safe. Terms like harm and human are too ambiguous to specify precisely.
7PKx3kS7f4A.why: Pointed to in AI safety debates as a short explanation of why encoding human values as simple rules is so hard.

7PoajCqNKpg.summary: Colin Smith introduces Structure and Interpretation of Classical Mechanics and his Clojure port, sicmutils. He shows how higher-order functions and a symbolic algebra system can represent Lagrangian mechanics.
7PoajCqNKpg.why: Recommended as the best introduction to SICM and sicmutils and a showcase of what such symbolic systems can do.

7W33HRc1A6c.summary: George Carlin's stand-up routine arguing the planet will be fine and it is people who are in trouble. It mocks the idea of saving the planet.
7W33HRc1A6c.why: HN quotes it in environmental threads as a famous, darkly funny take that the planet will outlast humanity.

7cC3_jGwl_U.summary: Cory Benfield's PyCon 2016 talk on building protocol libraries that can be reused widely, using the Python Hyper HTTP project as the example. He argues for separating protocol parsing from I/O.
7cC3_jGwl_U.why: HN points to it as the foundational argument for sans-I/O protocol library design.

7kQk9-KLPfU.summary: A doctor from Medlife Crisis explains in under three minutes why even a rich patient should not simply order every medical test, touching on pre-test probability and Bayesian reasoning. False positives make blanket testing counterproductive.
7kQk9-KLPfU.why: HN people link it as a short, funny and accurate explanation of why over-testing and over-screening can do harm.

7nL10C7FSbE.summary: A hands-on comparison of how jet fuel, diesel, heating oil, kerosene, avgas and gasoline burn and what color they are. It shows that gasoline ignites more easily than jet fuel.
7nL10C7FSbE.why: HN cites it as a practical demonstration that kerosene-type fuels are hard to ignite compared with gasoline.

7w4rg3UcsgI.summary: Tech Ingredients builds a larger solar-powered desiccant air conditioner that uses a calcium chloride liquid desiccant with evaporative cooling to cool their lab. The video includes the engineering calculations.
7w4rg3UcsgI.why: HN points to it as a detailed, DIY-able design for desiccant-based cooling.

7BGtVJ3lBdE.summary: A 60 Minutes report on neurosurgeon Ali Rezai using focused ultrasound on the brain to treat Alzheimer's and addiction. It shows experiments opening the blood-brain barrier and targeting addiction-related regions.
7BGtVJ3lBdE.why: HN cites it as a fascinating look at ultrasound-based brain treatments.

71eUes30gwc.summary: Kurzgesagt explores the idea that black holes could create universes and that we might live inside one. It builds up the physics of how density falls as black holes get larger.
71eUes30gwc.why: HN refers to it for the notion that big black holes are not very dense and that universes could form inside black holes.

75Ju0eM5T2c.summary: A five-minute clip from Donald Knuth's Web of Stories interviews in which he gives advice to young people, including being wary when too many people adopt an idea.
75Ju0eM5T2c.why: HN quotes it as a source for Knuth's caution against believing something is good just because it is trendy.

79fgH08z6xs.summary: minimme traces the timeline of 3D graphics engines on the Game Boy Advance, from early experiments to commercial 3D games, covering techniques such as voxel rendering. It is a history and showcase of what developers coaxed out of the limited hardware.
79fgH08z6xs.why: HN people recommend it as the best overview of how 3D on the GBA progressed over the console's life, usually in threads about GBA ports and homebrew 3D engines.

7K5p_tBcrd0.summary: Historian Doron Swade tells the story of Charles Babbage's quest to build the Difference Engine and the construction of Difference Engine No. 2 at the Science Museum. The talk covers Babbage's motivation, his machines and Ada Lovelace's insight into the Analytical Engine.
7K5p_tBcrd0.why: HN commenters link it as a source on Babbage's machines, especially for the section around minute 36 on Ada Lovelace's insight beyond numeric computation.

7TqqdOcX4dc.summary: A side-by-side edit lining up footage of the Wuppertal Schwebebahn suspended monorail filmed in 1902 and in 2015. It lets you compare how the buildings and surroundings changed over 113 years.
7TqqdOcX4dc.why: HN shares it whenever the Wuppertal suspended railway comes up, as a neat then-and-now comparison.

7XUWpze_A_s.summary: A five-minute demo of a live ClojureScript game editor by Chris Granger. It is based on Bret Victor's demo from the Inventing on Principle talk, with code changes reflected instantly in the running game.
7XUWpze_A_s.why: Cited as an early example of live coding applied beyond debugging, and as precursor to Light Table.

7YpFGkG-u1w.summary: Casey Muratori's invited lecture on where bad code comes from, rebroadcast from a Twitch stream. He critiques conventional wisdom such as SOLID and Clean Code and argues about how those habits lead to slow, poorly structured software.
7YpFGkG-u1w.why: HN commenters cite it as a sharp critique of SOLID, Clean Code and 'non-pessimized' programming, and as context for why software is getting worse.

7aXbh9VUB3U.summary: Ben Eater explains how the PS/2 keyboard interface works, covering its clocked serial protocol and scancodes. He builds up the hardware-level understanding needed to read keypresses.
7aXbh9VUB3U.why: HN commenters point to it as the clearest explanation of the PS/2 protocol, usually when keyboard interfaces come up.

7d9juPsv1QU.summary: The Academy's 2014 Sci-Tech Awards segment honoring Matt Pharr, Greg Humphreys and Pat Hanrahan for their physically based rendering work and book. The authors give a short acceptance speech that thanks Donald Knuth for literate programming.
7d9juPsv1QU.why: HN points to it as proof that the Physically Based Rendering book won an Oscar and for the speech crediting Knuth's literate programming.

7jPKEyM44GU.summary: A short video of the first TRON Smart House, built in 1989 as a demonstration of ubiquitous and ambient computing in the home. It comes from the uID Center, which promoted the TRON architecture.
7jPKEyM44GU.why: HN cites it as the concrete demo behind discussions of Japan's TRON project and early smart-home ideas.

7k1ehaE0bdU.summary: A nearly three-hour Joe Rogan interview with Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, covering Meta's products, AI, smart glasses, and his views on culture and company direction. The conversation is wide-ranging and long-form.
7k1ehaE0bdU.why: HN commenters cite it as a primary source for what Zuckerberg says in his own words, such as on AI writing most new code, WhatsApp, and Apple interoperability.

7lVAFcDX4eM.summary: A demo of a raycasting 3D engine built entirely from in-game mechanisms in vanilla Factorio 0.17. It renders simple 3D scenes, producing a new frame every 45 game ticks, with the video sped up to compensate for low UPS.
7lVAFcDX4eM.why: HN points to it as a showpiece of what Factorio's circuit network can compute, alongside other absurd in-game computing feats.

7lm3K8zVOdY.summary: A Clojure/conj 2014 talk by Lucas Cavalcanti and Edward Wible on four uses of Datomic. They cover HTTP caching, audit trails, mobile database sync and authorization, drawing on the immutable transaction log.
7lm3K8zVOdY.why: HN cites it as Nubank's account of building a bank on Datomic and Clojure, and for what Datomic's temporal model enables.

7mmlmxamw_k.summary: A clip from Joe Rogan Experience #928 in which Rogan, with Arian Foster, explains why he abandoned his belief in Moon landing conspiracy theories. He describes how doctored training photos fueled doubt before he learned more of the physics.
7mmlmxamw_k.why: Cited as an example of someone publicly changing their mind on the Moon landing hoax and of why skeptics had rational-seeming doubts.

7q9vIMXSTzc.summary: Jack Moffitt presents Servo, an experimental browser engine written in Rust and designed to be parallel at every level, using multiple cores, the GPU, fork-join concurrency and SIMD. The talk covers motivations, architecture and plans for the project.
7q9vIMXSTzc.why: HN commenters cite it as a detailed source on Servo's design and performance, including plans to move Servo code into Gecko.

7tScAyNaRdQ.summary: A short film adaptation of Terry Bisson's story 'They're Made Out of Meat', in which alien explorers discuss with disbelief that humans are sentient beings made of meat. It won a grand prize at the 2006 SIFF short film festival.
7tScAyNaRdQ.why: HN commenters recommend it as a well-made version of the story and quote it jokingly whenever discussions touch on biology versus machine intelligence.

70vYj1KPyT4.summary: Professor Dave critiques science communicator Sabine Hossenfelder, arguing that her content has drifted toward anti-establishment rhetoric. He frames it as commentary rather than a hit piece.
70vYj1KPyT4.why: HN mentions it only critically, as a rebuttal to Hossenfelder when her credibility is questioned.

74Ig_QKndvE.summary: A French-language documentary on the history of Prolog, created in Marseille by Alain Colmerauer in the early 1970s, with interviews of many people involved. It traces the origins of logic programming and later developments of the language.
74Ig_QKndvE.why: Cited in Prolog threads as a rare documentary on the language's origins, with proper subtitles despite being in French.

7DTlWPgX6zs.summary: Nicolai Josuttis's CppCon 2018 talk walks through the many forms of initialization in C++, including uniform initialization, and how their rules and effects differ. He argues the situation is confusing enough that nobody can say what to teach beginners.
7DTlWPgX6zs.why: Used mostly as a citation of C++'s historical baggage and complexity when HN criticizes or jokes about the language.

7GhAuZH6phs.summary: A short recording of a 1565 organ in Mantua tuned in quarter-comma meantone, showing split sharps in use. The extra keys provide separate D-sharp and A-flat for more tonalities.
7GhAuZH6phs.why: Used as a concrete example of split-key instruments and an audible demonstration of the D-sharp versus E-flat difference.

7MFtl2XXnUc.summary: A That Mitchell and Webb Look sketch in which a customer tries to buy a gift for his aunt in a shop that keeps pushing him toward extras.
7MFtl2XXnUc.why: Invoked as a joke when discussing ad creep, second screens and overbearing commercial or online experiences.

7O4V7JfeTSU.summary: Footage of the failed Mercury-Redstone 1 launch, where the engine cut off almost immediately after liftoff. The escape tower and parachutes then deployed because the rocket thought the flight was over.
7O4V7JfeTSU.why: Cited as the canonical footage of the famous four-inch flight, usually when discussing aborted launches.

7Ooa7wOKHhg.summary: CNN report on bodycam footage of former Mesa police officer Philip Brailsford shooting unarmed Daniel Shaver in an Arizona hotel. Brailsford was later acquitted of murder charges.
7Ooa7wOKHhg.why: HN cites it as a stark example in discussions of police use of force and accountability.

7Xad5Rl0N2E.summary: A one-minute clip from Monty Python's Life of Brian in which revolutionaries grudgingly list everything the Romans have done for them, from roads to clean water. It is a satirical sketch about refusing to credit a disliked group.
7Xad5Rl0N2E.why: HN commenters quote it jokingly whenever someone lists the unacknowledged benefits of an entity people love to complain about.

7Ys_yKGNFRQ.summary: The Slow Mo Guys visit a lab with a camera capable of filming at 10 trillion frames per second, fast enough to see light travel. They show the setup and the resulting footage.
7Ys_yKGNFRQ.why: Used as the standard reference whenever HN discusses filming light or ultrafast cameras.

7bXJ_obaiYQ.summary: A one-minute clip from the film Minority Report showing digital signage that recognizes a passerby and personalizes ads to him by name. It depicts a vision of targeted advertising driven by biometric identification.
7bXJ_obaiYQ.why: HN uses it as the go-to reference whenever a story involves ad tracking, facial recognition or personalized billboards.

7cNg_ifibCQ.summary: Louis Rossmann explains why many 16-inch MacBook Pros fail and are difficult to repair, focusing on power design on the logic board. He argues the design leads to failures that are hard to fix.
7cNg_ifibCQ.why: HN mentions are mostly critical or incidental, using it in discussions of Apple hardware design and repairability rather than recommending it.

7d59O6cfaM0.summary: Microsoft Research demonstrates holoportation, which reconstructs and compresses high-quality 3D models of people in real time and sends them anywhere. With a HoloLens, remote participants appear as if present in your room.
7d59O6cfaM0.why: Cited as the benchmark demo for telepresence and photorealistic avatars, in discussions of remote work and VR.

7gRsgkdfYJ8.summary: A short clip from the 2013 LinuxCon Linux Kernel Panel in which Linus Torvalds is asked about being approached to insert a backdoor into Linux. He answers no verbally while nodding yes, which became a much-shared moment.
7gRsgkdfYJ8.why: Cited as the source clip whenever threads discuss government pressure, backdoors, or trust in the Linux kernel.

7qZl_5xHoBw.summary: A long Joe Rogan Experience podcast episode with Elon Musk covering his businesses and views on a range of topics. It includes discussion of tariffs and a talk about video games.
7qZl_5xHoBw.why: HN mostly cites it as a source for what Musk said, such as on tariffs or gaming, and for context on Rogan's political endorsement rather than recommending it.

7s664NsLeFM.summary: A very short clip of Carl Sagan saying that to make an apple pie from scratch you must first invent the universe. It illustrates how everything depends on a chain of prior things.
7s664NsLeFM.why: HN commenters use the quote as shorthand in arguments about abstractions, standing on others' work and the limits of building from scratch.

7tAYXQPWdC0.summary: A 1978 documentary hosted by Leonard Nimoy about the coming ice age, reposted with a framing that contrasts it with today's climate science.
7tAYXQPWdC0.why: HN commenters mostly cite it skeptically in climate threads, as an example of past predictions of cooling.

7xH7eGFuSYI.summary: A four-minute Adam Ruins Everything segment on why employers discourage workers from sharing salaries. It argues that discussing pay with coworkers is legal and helps workers.
7xH7eGFuSYI.why: Linked in threads on pay and compensation as a quick explanation of why talking about salary helps employees.
